metadata.title: التقرير الوطني الأردني عن الدراسة الدولية للرياضيات والعلوم (TIMSS 2019)
metadata.venue: National Center for Human Resources Development (NCHRD) / IEA

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Jordanian student data drawn from MOE, private, and UNRWA schools. Sampling was implemented as a two-stage probability proportional-to-size (PPS) design at the school level, followed by random selection of one Grade 8 class/section within each sampled school. The report explicitly states that sampling weights were computed and taken into account in the analysis (e.g., weighted percentages for location, school gender, and sampling strata). It does not report replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty estimation details are not fully specified in the text provided.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a national descriptive report summarizing TIMSS 2019 results (means, rankings, and achievement-level distributions) rather than an empirical predictive modeling study. The dependent outcomes are reported as TIMSS achievement scale scores and achievement-level percentages, and the report does not document any plausible-values (PV) workflow or missing-data handling strategy. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported in the provided text, and the extraction cannot infer a specific PV combination or imputation/deletion rule.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 Jordanian national sample selected from MOE schools, private schools, and UNRWA schools. The sampling unit was the school (two-stage PPS sampling), and within each selected school one Grade 8 section was randomly selected. The report provides the final sample as 235 schools and 7176 students; no additional student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., item completion thresholds or missing-data exclusions) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This Jordanian national report documents TIMSS 2019 Grade 8 performance in Mathematics and Science using a two-stage PPS sampling design across MOE, private, and UNRWA schools. The report describes the assessment structure (multiple-choice and constructed-response items), content domains (e.g., Number, Algebra, Geometry, Data & Probability for Mathematics; Physics, Biology, Chemistry, Earth Science for Science), and cognitive domains (Knowing, Applying, Reasoning). For Science, Jordan’s mean score is 452 versus the international mean 490, with Jordan ranking 31st among participating countries and 5th among Arab countries; for Mathematics, Jordan’s mean is 420 versus 489 internationally, ranking 33rd and 5th among Arab countries. The report also reports statistically significant improvement from TIMSS 2015 to TIMSS 2019: +26 points in Science and +36 points in Mathematics at the national level, and it highlights subgroup disparities by gender, location (city/rural), and school authority. Because this is a descriptive national reporting document, no student-level ML models, PV combination method, or missing-data handling procedure is provided in the text.
